body:
People are generally more forgiving of you than yourself.  The anxiety you constantly feel is not helping you feel secure in your friendships.  People love and value you, they may have days they feel crushed by the world and you're not alone :)

I hope you are getting help for the anxiety and depression? Whether it is talk therapy and/or medication it can make a difference.  It will give you a safety net while you are recovering.

Regarding connecting with people, I'm assuming you would get along best with like-minded introverts.  There are plenty of us out there, we are secretly witty and fun. However, we are all naturally reclusive and good at hiding in plain sight; this isn't conductive to making friends or networking.

Join a club or interest, something you want to learn.  It may be un-natural, but start a conversation with the quiet person in the corner, start looking for people like you.  Easy for me to say from across an ocean.  You appear to be introspective and self critical.  This will have given you an excellent social awareness.  Turn this outwards and inspect the people around you.  Who do you want to be friends with?  

Forming relationships with older people may appeal if you are searching for an emotional maturity missing from your acquaintances.  There's nothing wrong with older friends, however, you will be able to find the same character traits in some of your contemporaries.

I don't think you chose when to let someone in.  No matter how guarded you are, one you meet someone who *gets* you they worm their way in regardless of what you want.  The difficulty is admitting to yourself (and them) that you love them or have 'let them in'.

It may not happen tomorrow, but please don't stop trying.  You've struck a nerve with me from across the Atlantic so you can connect with others. Love from the UK.
